proposals.new_text:
---
title: "Why do I open my banking app, see the balance, and close it before I've actually looked?"
pubDate: "2026-09-19"
description: "You check. You don't look. There is a difference, and you know it."
draft: false
---

You open the app because you feel like you should. You see a number. You close it before the number means anything. Then you put the phone face-down.

That is not laziness. It is a system you built, probably somewhere around the first time the number was worse than you expected and you had to go and do the rest of your day anyway.

Joel sees this in almost every first conversation he has with clients who earn well and save nothing. Not people who are careless with money. People who are careful with everything else and have one blind spot that sits quietly behind a login screen.

The thing you are avoiding is not the balance. It is the conversation the balance would start — about the ISA you said you would open in January, the pension you have been meaning to look at, the subscription you know is still running.

Checking without looking keeps all of that at a distance. It lets you say, honestly, that you did check. It costs you nothing in the moment and roughly everything across a decade.

If this is the pattern, the starting point is not a budget. It is a ten-minute honest reckoning with what you are actually afraid you will find. Joel's MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner background is built around exactly this kind of quiet awareness — not the numbers, the story beneath the numbers.
